record.context_brief: Parameterized game strategies in generalized Hex
record.original_question: In Generalized Hex played on an undirected graph G with distinguished vertices v1 and v2, two players alternately place white and black pebbles on previously unoccupied vertices, player one moving first and winning if the white vertices contain a path from v1 to v2. Given G, v1, v2, and a positive integer k, does player one have a winning strategy that succeeds within at most k of player one's moves?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Generalized Hex is the following two-player game. The board is an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ together with two distinguished vertices $v_1,v_2 \in V$. Players (player one and player two) move alternately, with player one moving first. On each move, the moving player places a pebble of his own color (white for player one, black for player two) on a previously unoccupied vertex of $G$. Player one wins as soon as the set of white vertices contains a path from $v_1$ to $v_2$ in $G$; otherwise player two wins.

Short Generalized Hex: Given an undirected graph $G$, distinguished vertices $v_1, v_2 \in V(G)$, and a positive integer $k$, decide whether player one has a winning strategy that guarantees a win within at most $k$ of his own moves.

When parameterized by $k$, determine the parameterized complexity of this decision problem: is it fixed-parameter tractable, and where exactly does it lie in the parameterized complexity hierarchy (e.g., W[1], W[2], …, AW[*])?
artifact.status_search_result: Bonnet, Jamain and Saffidine (ICALP 2017, "The Parameterized Complexity of Positional Games") proved that Short Generalized Hex is W[1]-complete when parameterized by the number of moves, resolving this open problem of Downey and Fellows. They also show membership in AW[*] was previously known and that Short Hex on the hexagonal grid is FPT.

status_evidence.title: The Parameterized Complexity of Positional Games
status_evidence.snippet: Short Generalized Hex is W[1]-complete parameterized by the number of moves, solving an open problem from the influential list of open problems of Downey and Fellows (1999).
status_evidence.claim: Short Generalized Hex parameterized by number of moves is W[1]-complete, resolving the Downey–Fellows open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Parameterized Complexity of Positional Games (LIPIcs ICALP 2017)
status_evidence.snippet: For Generalized Hex, played on an arbitrary graph, the short game is W[1]-hard and in AW[*].
status_evidence.claim: The short Generalized Hex game is W[1]-complete and lies in AW[*].
